title: context-field-catalogue.v1
description: The closed, typed catalogue of every decision-context path a rule may address (A§55, plan §7 DEC-1). It is the vocabulary of the rule DSL: `rule-set.v1.json` leaf conditions carry a `field`, and DEC-4 rejects a rule whose `field` is not in the catalogue — naming the offending path — so a typo is a publish-time 400 rather than a silently-false condition in production. It also declares the comparison type and unit per path, which is how `platform/ruledsl` (LIB-9) knows to compare `delinquency.amountOverdue` as a decimal rather than as text. This file is the *shape*; the v1 catalogue *content* is `examples/decisioning/context-field-catalogue.v1.example.json`, which enumerates every addressable leaf of `context-document.v1.json` and is the artefact services load. Paths whose value is an array (`provenance[]`) are deliberately not addressable: the DSL has no quantifiers, which is what keeps it non-Turing-complete, deterministic and parity-testable (A§88).

catalogueVersion.description: Version of the catalogue *content*, starting at 1 and incremented whenever a field is added, removed or re-typed. Recorded alongside every published rule set so an audit can replay a decision against the vocabulary that was in force. A removal or a type change is breaking for rules that reference the path, so it ships with the corresponding rule-set major version.

fields.description: Every addressable context path, in document order (subject, delinquency, account, customer, arrangement, contactHistory). `path` is unique across the array — DEC-4 rejects a catalogue with duplicates, because two entries for one path make the comparison type ambiguous.

field.title: CatalogueField
field.description: One addressable context path with the comparison semantics the rule engine applies to it.

path.description: Dot path of the value inside a `context-document.v1.json` instance, e.g. `delinquency.dpd`. Always at least two segments deep: the top level of a context document holds sections only, never scalars. Matches the `field` value of a rule-set leaf condition byte for byte.

type.description: Comparison type, not JSON encoding. `number` values are compared as arbitrary-precision decimals (LIB-9 uses shopspring/decimal), which is why `delinquency.amountOverdue` — a decimal *string* on the wire — is catalogued as `number`: rules read `"500.00"` and compare it exactly. `date` covers both calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and RFC3339 UTC timestamps and compares chronologically. `string` compares by exact equality and set membership only (no substring, no regex, no case folding). `boolean` compares only to `true`/`false`.

unit.description: Unit of a `number` field, mandatory reading for anyone writing a threshold. `majorUnits` is a currency amount in major units (EUR 500.00 = `"500.00"`), the one deliberate departure from the platform's minor-unit rule and only inside context documents (contracts/README.md §4). `days` is a whole number of days. `count` is a whole number of occurrences. Omitted for `string`, `boolean` and `date` fields, which have no unit.

description.description: What the field means, who produces it, and any nullability — written for the business analyst authoring a rule and the auditor reading a decision explanation, not for a developer.

allOf.title: unit is meaningful only for numbers
allOf.description: A unit on a string, boolean or date field would be dead metadata that a rule author could mistake for a conversion instruction, so it is rejected.
